evidence: ForwardCommandController doc (control.ros.org) states each instance claims `joint[i] + "/" + interface_name`; with joints=["joint1"] and interface_name="position" both controllers claim the token "joint1/position", and ros2_control#345 confirms that two controllers claiming the same command interface conflict because command interfaces are exclusively owned (resource manager enforces single-claimer rule).

fmauch's comment on ros-controls/ros2_control#1179 states: 'define two controllers claiming the same interface, e.g. all joints' position interface' and shows the error 'Command interface jointXYZ/position is already claimed' — both controllers declare the same exclusive joint position command interface token.

franka_hardware/ros2_control/franka_ros2_control_macros.xacro (frankaemika/franka_ros2 humble): configure_arm_joints macro emits joint_name="${joint_prefix}_joint{1..7}" each with <command_interface name="effort"/>; franka_hardware_interface.cpp exports tokens as joint.name+"/"+cmd_interface.name; the two arm instances resolve joint_prefix to "panda_1" and "panda_3" respectively, yielding fully disjoint token sets with no shared exclusive resource.

producer_frame: galactic+: on_init() added as pure virtual (virtual CallbackReturn on_init()=0) in ControllerInterface/ControllerInterfaceBase; init() signature expanded to pass controller_name, urdf, cm_update_rate, node_namespace, node_options; configure() remains as non-virtual lifecycle-transition wrapper
consumer_frame: foxy-era controller: does NOT override on_init() (method did not exist in foxy ControllerInterface); calls configure() via lifecycle and overrides update(); depends on init(controller_name) or init(controller_name, node_options) two-arg signature
evidence: GitHub ros-controls/ros2_control foxy branch controller_interface.hpp: on_init() absent, configure() present; galactic branch controller_interface.hpp: on_init() declared pure virtual (= 0), making any consumer that omits its override an abstract class — verified via control.ros.org galactic API source and direct GitHub branch fetch

producer_frame: mavros 0.15.x: CommandPlugin (command.cpp) advertised ROS service \"guided_enable\" (CommandBool); command.py exposed guided_enable proxy attribute
consumer_frame: mavros/scripts/mavsetp called command.guided_enable(value=True) in enable_offboard() to request OFFBOARD/guided mode
evidence: Commit d7bd7857 (mavlink/mavros, landed in v0.16.0, fix for issue #407) removed guided_enable service from CommandPlugin (command.cpp) and removed guided_enable from command.py; consumer mavsetp still called command.guided_enable(value=True) causing the 'module object has no attribute guided_enable' error reported in issue #478, confirmed by commit bdda1fab which fixed the consumer in v0.17.0.

producer_frame: sys_time plugin after commit e1a80052fb (fix #206): reads conn/system_time, conn/timesync, time/frame_id, time/time_ref_source, time/timesync_avg_alpha
consumer_frame: px4_config.yaml (unchanged in same commit): sets conn_timesync and conn_system_time as flat top-level keys (old names without slash namespace)
evidence: Commit e1a80052fb (mavlink/mavros, "plugin: sys_time: fix #206 (param ns)") shows the plugin changed from nh.param("conn_timesync",...) to nh.param("conn/timesync",...) and from nh.param("conn_system_time",...) to nh.param("conn/system_time",...), while px4_config.yaml in the same tree still sets the flat keys conn_timesync and conn_system_time.

producer_frame: user-chosen TF frame (arbitrary header.frame_id in goal_constraints[].position_constraints[].header, e.g. "ur_base_link")
consumer_frame: robot_model->getModelFrame() (enforced by PILZ computePoseIK equality check, typically "world")
evidence: moveit2 trajectory_functions.cpp (Humble API source) line ~70: `if (frame_id != robot_model->getModelFrame()) { RCLCPP_ERROR ... "Given frame (...) is unequal to model frame(...)" return false; }` — producer's open frame_id field vs. consumer's hard equality check against the model frame, confirmed by issue #3035 error "Given frame (ur_base_link) is unequal to model frame(world)".

consumer_frame: global_frame (costmap global_frame parameter, default "map", read via costmap_ros->getGlobalFrameID())
evidence: nav2_navfn_planner/src/navfn_planner.cpp sets global_frame_ = costmap_ros->getGlobalFrameID() (default "map" per costmap docs); ComputePathToPose.action goal is geometry_msgs/PoseStamped whose header.frame_id is caller-supplied (api.nav2.org/actions/jazzy/computepathtopose.html); both default to "map" so no fixed-frame incompatibility at the interface level.

producer_frame: Iron: controller_server exposes parameter progress_checker_plugins (list of strings)
consumer_frame: Humble consumer config reads parameter progress_checker_plugin (single string)
evidence: PR ros-navigation/navigation2#3555 body explicitly shows the breaking rename: Humble used `progress_checker_plugin: \"progress_checker\"` (string); Iron requires `progress_checker_plugins: [\"progress_checker\"]` (list), confirmed via `gh api repos/ros-planning/navigation2/pulls/3555`.

producer_frame: Humble nav2_msgs/action/Spin goal: {target_yaw: float32, time_allowance: builtin_interfaces/Duration}; result: {total_elapsed_time}; feedback: {angular_distance_traveled}
consumer_frame: Iron/Jazzy nav2_behavior_tree spin_action.cpp sets goal_.disable_collision_checks, goal_.target_yaw, goal_.time_allowance
evidence: GitHub issue #5633 and api.nav2.org confirm Humble Spin.action goal has only target_yaw+time_allowance; Iron/Jazzy adds bool disable_collision_checks (PR #3891); nav2_behavior_tree/plugins/action/spin_action.cpp on main explicitly sets goal_.disable_collision_checks, confirming the consumer references the added field.

producer_frame: Galactic: Client::async_send_request(SharedRequest) returns SharedFuture (std::shared_future<SharedResponse>); Humble: returns FutureAndRequestId (struct with std::future<SharedResponse> and int64_t request_id, with deprecated implicit conversion to SharedFuture)
consumer_frame: Consumer stores the result of async_send_request into a SharedFuture variable and calls .get() on it, depending on the return being directly assignable to SharedFuture
evidence: rclcpp PR#1734 (github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/1734) changed async_send_request return from SharedFuture to FutureAndRequestId in Humble; moveit2_tutorials issue #122 confirms existing consumers storing result as SharedFuture trigger a deprecation warning \"use .future.share() instead of an implicit conversion\"
